summary: Cache-side memory pressure and poorly hidden load latency limit the kernel, rather than DRAM bandwidth.
reasoning: Memory SOL is 64.89% versus 52.2% compute SOL. L2 throughput reaches 71.13% of active-cycle peak, while DRAM throughput is only 19.56%, consistent with the 93.51% L2 hit rate. Long-scoreboard stalls indicate substantial waiting for memory dependencies.

root_causes.cause: Global loads use only half of each transferred sector, increasing cache traffic for the operand tiles.

evidence.interpretation: Global-load sector utilization is only 50%, indicating inefficient use of transferred data.
L2 is the most heavily utilized measured memory level.

fixes.fix: Profile A and B loads separately and tune their tile layouts for the actual input strides, making adjacent lanes access contiguous, aligned elements.
fixes.rationale: Improving sector utilization reduces cache traffic per useful operand byte and relieves L2 pressure.

root_causes.cause: Low achieved occupancy limits the ability to hide operand-load latency; register and shared-memory usage constrain residency.

evidence.interpretation: Few resident active warps are available to cover memory latency.
Warps frequently wait for outstanding memory dependencies.
Register usage contributes to the reported five-block residency limit.
Shared memory also limits residency to five blocks per SM.

fixes.fix: Extend autotuning with smaller accumulator tiles and lower-stage variants, selecting configurations that improve occupancy without introducing spills or losing necessary load overlap.
fixes.rationale: Reducing both register and shared-memory footprints can allow more resident warps to hide load latency.
